text:
alex_ong: Heads up — we’re seeing a cluster of EU-CENTRAL GPU racks return weird OOB sensor values after last night’s sensor firmware push. Provisioning is backing up for new nodes.

maria_chen: Ugh. What are the sensor symptoms? temp spikes, NaNs, voltages?

alex_ong: Mostly temps jumping to -128 or 65535 in the BMC sensor table, then the provisioning service marks the node unhealthy and retries. A few nodes also failed soft-reboot via IPMI.

devon: Can you paste the raw ipmi output? I want to see which sensor IDs are affected.

alex_ong: Sure — sample from node gpu-eu3-17:

```
# ipmitool -I lanplus -H 10.2.17.9 -U admin -P **** sensor list
CPU Temp | -128 | degrees C | ns  | no reading
GPU Temp | 65535 | degrees C | ns | no reading
System Temp | 46 | degrees C | ok |  
```

samir: That looks like the sensor firmware is returning sentinel/overflow values. Could be endian or scaling change in the firmware image.

infra-bot: Deploy job "sensor-fw-v2.3.1" completed in eu-central at 02:10 UTC (job id: deploy-55321). 18 devices updated.

maria_chen: infra-bot — can you list which serial ranges were in that batch? We need to correlate.

infra-bot: serial ranges: EU3-RACK-A[12-29], EU3-RACK-B[01-06], EU3-RACK-C[05-10]

devon: Ok, that matches failing hosts. Quick mitigation options: (1) rollback sensor-fw to v2.3.0 for those racks, (2) add a provisioning gate to skip BMC sensor check for ~24h, or (3) whitelist nodes and continue but mark capacity degraded.

ops-oncall: Don’t whitelist unless we accept risk. If IPMI soft-reboots are failing we could leave nodes in a half-provisioned state and waste capacity. I vote rollback.

alex_ong: Agreed. Rolling back is safest. Maria — can you open a rollback job? We should also mute alerts for spurious temp values in metrics so we don't get paged.

maria_chen: Opening rollback job now. Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/oob-fw-rollback (see section 'selective rollback'). I’ll target EU3-RACK-A/B first and pause further sensor-fw deployments.

samir: Also add a temporary health-check override in the provisioner: ignore temp sensor if value < -100 or > 60000. That'll stop churn while rollback happens.

devon: I’ll push a small patch to provisioning gate to treat those sentinel values as 'sensor-unavailable' instead of FAIL. Patching now and will run integration in staging.

alex_ong: Estimated timeline: rollback batch1 (A/B) — 30m, monitor 30m, rollback C if needed. Will update capacity dashboard and reduce autoscaler target to avoid re-scheduling degraded nodes.

infra-bot: rollback job "sensor-fw-rollback-1878004321" queued (targets: EU3-RACK-A[12-29], EU3-RACK-B[01-06]). ETA 10m.

maria_chen: Paging release-eng to halt the global sensor-fw rollout until we have a postmortem. @release-eng @firmware-team

samir: Quick reminder: if we rollback BMC firmware we should also ensure secure boot signatures match — some of the newer images changed signature layout. Check runbook step 4.

alex_ong: Good call. Maria, include signature verification in the rollback job.

maria_chen: Done. Also adding a cost note: if this blocks provisioning for >2h we’ll notify sales about potential capacity shortfall for new Dedicated commitments in EU-CENTRAL.

ops-oncall: I’ll stay on this until rollback completes. If anything flips to CI/CD rate limits let me know.

devon: Patch to provisioner gate pushed: PR #4217. Applying as hotfix to eu-central staging and then prod after smoke.

alex_ong: Thanks all. Update in 15. If rollback shows no regressions we can re-release after smaller canary and additional unit tests for sensor value ranges. :thumbsup:
